_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Dynamic Response Analysis and Test Report
summary: Describes the ground and flight analyses and tests used to characterize a system's elastic response to dynamic load inputs, verifying the dynamic loads and fatigue loads spectrum, with results used to determine service life for operational usage.
use_relationship:
The Dynamic Response Analysis and Test Report describes the ground and flight analyses and tests used to characterize the system elastic response to dynamic load inputs.  It provides a means for verifying or improving the dynamic loads analysis and fatigue loads spectrum for the air vehicle, missile, or helicopter weapon system.  Results are incorporated into the fatigue test program to determine service life for actual operational usage.

a.  This Data Item Description (DID) is applicable to any contract for which a dynamic response test is required.

b.  This DID contains the format, content, and intended use information for the data deliverable resulting from the work task described in section 5 of MIL-STD-1530, Aircraft Structural Integrity Program (ASIP) (copies of this document are available online at https://quicksearch.dla.mil).
distribution_statement: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

preparation_instructions.title: Reference Documents
preparation_instructions.content: The applicable issue of the documents cited herein, including their approval dates and dates of any applicable amendments, notices, and revisions, shall be as specified in the contract.

preparation_instructions.title: Format
preparation_instructions.content: The Dynamic Response Analysis and Test Report shall be in the contractor's format.

preparation_instructions.title: Content
preparation_instructions.content: The Dynamic Response Analysis and Test Report shall describe the contractor's analyses and testing activities associated with the design for dynamic load inputs. The report shall contain the results and findings used to validate or correct the initial dynamic response analyses.

children.title: The report shall be based on the interpretation
children.content: and evaluation of the dynamic response analyses and tests and shall contain the following, as applicable:

children.title: Descriptions and photographs of the system
children.content: fixturing, rigging, ground equipment, instrumentation, component(s) under test, and the configurations including fuel states, store loadings, weights, centers-of-gravity, internal payloads, and simulated sling loads.

children.title: Descriptions of the flight or ground handling conditions
children.content: that result in significant dynamic responses of the structure, and the effects of these conditions on service life.

children.title: Descriptions of the test procedures
children.content: test conditions, test methods, and data acquisition systems, including a copy of the final version of the test plan.

children.title: Descriptions of the methodologies used for selecting
children.content: test instrumentation types, test instrumentation measurement capabilities, and test measurement locations.

children.title: Description of the methods used for mounting instrumentation
Descriptions of the methods used for the reduction and analysis of the test data
Copy of the test matrix as planned to be executed
Defined measurement units including axis labels of plots and figures
Plots of the transfer functions versus frequency for vibration sensors
Descriptions and time history plots of critical test load cases
Copy of the test log as executed
Results from both discrete and power spectral density methods
children.content: of analysis and a comparison of the load inputs, structural responses, and transfer functions with the dynamic loads analysis.

children.title: The transfer functions between the internal structural loads
children.content: and accelerations at various locations throughout the airframe and the gust, landing, taxi, takeoff, towing, buffet, aerial refueling, catapult, arrestment, gun fire, and store ejection load inputs.

children.title: The transfer functions between vertical center of gravity
children.content: accelerations and the load frequency distribution for the range of gross weights, system configurations, speeds, angles of attack, angles of sideslip, and altitudes being flown in service.
